options.text: The change in inherited characteristics of a population over successive generations
The process of an organism adapting within its lifetime
The growth and development of an individual organism
The extinction of species over time

questions.explanation: Evolution is the change in the inherited characteristics of a population over successive generations. It occurs through changes in allele frequencies caused by natural selection acting on variation within a population.

questions.stem: What did Charles Darwin observe about finches on the Galapagos Islands?

options.text: All finches were identical across all islands
Finches could not survive on the islands
Different islands had finches with different beak shapes adapted to local food sources
Finches had evolved from reptiles

questions.explanation: Darwin observed that different islands had different species of finches with beaks adapted to different food sources. This suggested they shared a common ancestor but had adapted to local conditions, helping Darwin develop his theory of natural selection.

questions.stem: Which of the following is evidence for evolution?

options.text: Fossils showing gradual changes in organisms over time
All organisms are identical
All organisms were created at the same time
Species never change over time

questions.explanation: Fossils provide strong evidence for evolution by showing gradual changes in organisms over millions of years. The fossil record shows how species have changed, how new species have appeared, and how others have gone extinct.

questions.stem: In what year did Darwin publish 'On the Origin of Species'?
questions.explanation: Darwin published 'On the Origin of Species' in 1859. Although he had developed his ideas much earlier during his voyage on HMS Beagle (1831-1836), he spent many years gathering evidence before publishing.

questions.stem: Why was Darwin's theory controversial when it was first proposed?

options.text: Because it had no evidence to support it
Because Darwin was not a real scientist
Because it challenged the religious belief that God created all species
Because scientists already had a better explanation

questions.explanation: Darwin's theory was controversial because it challenged the widely held religious belief that God created all species in their current form. Additionally, the mechanism of inheritance was not yet understood, making some scientists sceptical.

questions.stem: Which scientist independently developed a theory of evolution similar to Darwin's?

options.text: Gregor Mendel
Robert Hooke
Alfred Russel Wallace
Louis Pasteur

questions.explanation: Alfred Russel Wallace independently developed a theory of evolution by natural selection very similar to Darwin's. Wallace's letter to Darwin in 1858 prompted Darwin to finally publish his own work.

questions.stem: What was Lamarck's idea about evolution?

options.text: Evolution occurs through natural selection
Species do not change over time
Characteristics acquired during an organism's lifetime could be inherited
Evolution is driven by random mutations only

questions.explanation: Lamarck proposed that organisms could pass on characteristics they acquired during their lifetime to their offspring. This idea has been largely rejected because we now know that only changes in DNA (not acquired traits) can be inherited.
